title: Demo mode can still fire real authenticated-API writes: /settings is reachable by manual navigation and its submit handlers (profile, password, notification preference, account deletion) are neither intercepted by demo_update nor demo-branched in update_inner
evidence:
client.gleam:4710-4726: `UserSubmittedProfile -> { ... settings_api.update_profile(
            name: model.profile_name,
            phone: model.profile_phone,
            company_name: model.profile_company_name,
            rtb_number: model.profile_rtb_number,
            csrf_token: model.csrf_token,
            on_response: ApiReturnedProfileUpdate,
          ),` — no case model.demo_mode guard. Same shape at 4559 (settings_api.change_password), 4424 (settings_api.update_notification_preference), 4781 (settings_api.delete_account). `grep -n "UserSubmittedProfile\|UserSubmittedPasswordChange\|UserChangedNotificationPreference\|UserConfirmedAccountDeletion" client/src/demo/demo_update.gleam` returns nothing, so demo_update's `_ -> fallback(model, msg)` passes them to update_inner. BrowserChangedUrl with demo_mode=True and a non-public route runs `handle_browser_change(model, uri, route)` leaving demo_mode=True, and view dispatch `routes.Settings -> settings.view_settings(model)` (client.gleam:6454) has no demo guard; settings.gleam:318 wires `event.on_click(UserSubmittedProfile)`. The shell only hides the link (chunk-c shell.gleam: `case model.demo_mode { True -> element.none() ...`).
detail: An ungated demo visitor who navigates to /settings directly gets a working settings page whose submits fire real POSTs to live /api/v1 endpoints. Server-side auth + HMAC CSRF (csrf.gleam validate_token) reject the mock 'demo-csrf-token', so no data is written or leaked, but the 'demo mode issues no writes to real endpoints' pillar is breached client-side and the demo/ grep lint cannot catch it.
recommended_fix: Intercept UserSubmittedProfile/UserSubmittedPasswordChange/UserChangedNotificationPreference/UserConfirmedAccountDeletion in demo_update (no-op or store-local), or redirect non-public routes to the demo dashboard while demo_mode is True.

title: Fixture uses a famous real person's name (Grace Kelly) for a rejected applicant with eviction history and arrears; one phone number (087 123 4567) sits outside the 555 fictional range used everywhere else
evidence: Line 93: `const app_grace_json = "{\"id\":\"a-grace\",\"vacancy_id\":\"v-maples\",\"first_name\":\"Grace\",\"last_name\":\"Kelly\",\"email\":\"grace.kelly@example.ie\",...\"is_smoker\":true,\"has_eviction_history\":true,\"eviction_details\":\"Rent arrears, possession order settled in 2024\",\"has_ccjs\":true,...\"status\":\"rejected\"...}"`. Line 81 (Aoife): `\"phone\":\"087 123 4567\"` — every other fixture phone uses the 555 range (e.g. `\"087 555 0192\"`, `\"01 555 0172\"`).
detail: Grace Kelly is an identifiable real person (deceased actress/Princess of Monaco); attaching her name to a rejected, eviction-history tenant fixture is a reputational/privacy-craft miss against the 'no real persons' rule. 087 123 4567 is a real-prefix Irish mobile, unlike the 555-range numbers.
recommended_fix: Rename the a-grace fixture to a non-famous synthetic name and swap 087 123 4567 for a 555-range number for consistency with the rest of the dataset.
